initial_message: hi our hot water cylinder burst on thurs 24th sept about 6 in the morning and flooded the halway. carpet is soaked and the botom of the walls are wet. the plumber put a new cylinder in already. what do i need to do to claim

facts.policyholder.name: Sione Northbeck
facts.incident.description: Early on Thursday morning the hot water cylinder in the hallway cupboard burst at the bottom. Water soaked the cupboard floor and the hallway carpet and wet the bottom of the hallway walls. I turned off the water at the toby and the power to the cylinder. The plumber put in a new cylinder that morning.
facts.incident.cause: The hot water cylinder failed at the base seam
facts.loss.description: Hallway carpet soaked over about 7 m2; cylinder cupboard floor swollen; bottom of the hallway wall linings and skirting water-damaged
facts.mitigation.emergency_action: Turned off the water at the toby and the cylinder power at the switchboard, and mopped up
facts.mitigation.temporary_repair: Flax Mere Plumbing & Gas replaced the cylinder on Thursday 24 September 2026
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the hallway carpet and the cupboard. Available now.
facts.evidence.attendance_note: The plumber's attendance note. Available now.
facts.evidence.repair_quote: Quote from Upland Water Damage Services, total $3,645.50 including GST, dated 26 September 2026. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_previous_claims: Two. One in November last year when my car was hit in a car park, and one in February this year when the wind broke a window at home.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo of a narrow hallway with beige carpet soaked and darkened by water in front of an open cupboard door. Inside the cupboard the particle-board floor is swollen and a puddle has spread out onto the carpet; the bottom of the painted hallway wall lining and the white skirting board are water-stained and swollen. Morning light from a doorway at the end of the hall. The frame shows the carpet, the cupboard floor and the lower wall only.
materials.purpose: Shows the water damage in the hallway

data.found: Hot water cylinder in the hallway cupboard failed at the base seam. Cupboard floor and hallway carpet soaked.
data.work_done: Drained and removed the failed cylinder, installed a new 180 L electric cylinder, restored supply and tested. No further leak.
data.follow_up: Hallway carpet, cupboard floor and wall linings need drying and repair.

design.notes: Hint only: two other submitted claims in the past year (motor submitted 2025-11-10, home submitted 2026-02-12), neither the same event. The policy renewed on 1 September 2026, 23 days before the incident, but it was first taken out on 2019-09-01; a system that read the current period start as inception would wrongly add a second weak hit.

triage.rationale: Exactly one weak indicator (two other submitted claims in the past year), so a hint and standard, not a flag. Otherwise simple: cylinder replaced, nothing still leaking, home habitable, photo and complete quote (NZD 3,645.50 including GST). Coverage is not unclear: the pack policy carries no uncertainty marker in the lookup, and coverage = review_required on its own does not count (maintainer, 2026-09-30). The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: No receipt or ownership document in the pack

prior_claims_12m.basis: Two other submitted claims in the past year: motor submitted 2025-11-10 and home submitted 2026-02-12

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 September 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2019-09-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear. The current period started on 1 September 2026, 23 days before the incident, only because of a renewal.

possible_duplicate.basis: The earlier home claim (incident 2026-02-11) is months before this incident; the other is motor
